medications.name: metformin
medications.notes: Maximum dose, inadequate response per CGM. SLC22A1 AA predicts reduced hepatic uptake.

goals: Reduce HbA1c to below 8% as a first step

sideEffects.effect: persistent GI distress - diarrhea and nausea
sideEffects.notes: Patient has requested dosage review. SLC22A1 AA may explain both GI side effects and therapeutic failure.

lifestyle.diet: high-carbohydrate, frequent restaurant meals, low vegetable intake
lifestyle.sleep_quality: poor - frequent nocturia and nocturnal awakenings

snp_profile.pharmacogenomic_summary: TCF7L2 TT: highest genetic risk allele for T2D, impaired incretin/GLP-1 response - GLP-1RA may be particularly beneficial. SLC22A1 AA: reduced hepatic metformin transporter - explains clinical non-response. CYP2C19 GA: intermediate metabolizer (clinically minor for current regimen).

clinicianNotes: Patient has been on maximum-dose metformin for 4 years with inadequate glycemic control (HbA1c 9.2%). WHOOP data (avg recovery 31/100, avg HRV 22.8 ms) and CGM (TIR 18%, avg glucose 211 mg/dL) both confirm severe metabolic burden. Genomic profile explains failure: SLC22A1 AA reduces metformin hepatic uptake, TCF7L2 TT predicts impaired GLP-1 receptor response. Strong recommendation to switch primary agent. GLP-1 RA (semaglutide) is pharmacogenomically aligned and addresses obesity, CV risk, and renal concerns. CKD stage 3a eGFR 58 - SGLT-2i use with caution (threshold ~45 for empagliflozin). Refer to endocrinology.
alert_flags: MEDICATION_NON_RESPONSE: metformin - supported by SLC22A1 AA genotype and 4-year TIR <20%
CKD_MONITORING: eGFR 58 - SGLT-2i threshold, monitor creatinine quarterly
WHOOP_ALERT: avg recovery score 31 - severely impaired physiologic recovery
